q: How does Christ's resurrection benefit us?
a: By His resurrection Christ overcame death, shares righteousness with us, raises us to new life, and pledges our glorious resurrection

q: How were pious persons saved before the coming of Christ?
a: By believing in a Saviour to come.

q: What is required in the fifth Commandment?
a: Requireth preserving honour and performing duties in their several places and relations.

q: Why must He be a true and righteous man?
a: He must be truly human so human nature can pay for sin, and righteous so He can pay for others

q: To what does the forgiveness of sins necessarily lead?
a: The full enjoyment of a child of God's rights, access to the Father's fellowship, and eternal life

q: Why do you need Christ as a king?
a: Because I am weak and helpless.

q: According to Romans 5:10, how were we reconciled to God when we were His enemies?
a: Through the death of His Son

q: Did Adam act for himself alone in the covenant of works?
a: No; he represented all his posterity.

q: What is meant when we say Christ was our substitute?
a: Christ fulfilled God's law in my place and bore the punishment for my sins in my place.

q: Why do we call it the Kingdom of Grace?
a: Because in His kingdom our King reigns with grace and love, forgiving our sins.

q: What further benefit do we receive from Christ's sacrifice and death on the cross?
a: Through Christ's death our old nature is crucified with Him so we may offer ourselves as a sacrifice to Him

q: What is the true repentance or conversion of man?
a: It is the dying of the old nature and the coming to life of the new.

q: What does baptism represent?
a: Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ

q: How does Baptism save us from sin, death, and the devil?
a: In Baptism we come into fellowship with Christ, and are made partakers in His redemption

q: What does the baptizing with water signify?
a: The old man should be drowned by repentance with all sins; a new man shall live in righteousness forever

q: Why do the benefits of Christ's redemption become ours through baptism?
a: Because we are baptized into Christ's death, and the benefits belong to us through faith

q: To what does your baptism bind you?
a: To be a true follower of Christ.

q: How is the daily renewal accomplished?
a: The old man and sin are put away more and more; the new spiritual life appears in our conduct

q: What makes us certain that Christ is risen and lives forever?
a: God Himself tells us in His Word that Christ was raised from the dead and now lives forever, since death no longer has dominion over Him.

q: What hope has Christ secured for me?
a: To walk in newness of life in Christ, live in righteousness, and reign with Him forever.

q: What duty does baptism impose on those who receive it?
a: To drown the old sinful self through daily repentance, and let the new self in Christ grow in righteousness

q: What does baptism with water signify about the new man in us?
a: The new man should daily emerge and arise to live before God in righteousness and purity forever.

q: Since Christ has died for us, why do we still have to die?
a: Our death is not payment for our sins but ends sin and enters eternal life

q: What is sanctification?
a: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit

q: According to Romans 6:12, what must sin not do in our mortal body?
a: Reign

q: What special use is there of the moral law to the regenerate?
a: Regenerate delivered from law as covenant; law shows how bound to Christ for fulfilling it and enduring curse, provoking thankfulness

q: According to Romans 6:23, what are the wages of sin?
a: Death

q: What did Christ accomplish for us by His death on the cross?
a: By His death He has paid the wages of sin, which is death

q: Why is the service of sin and the devil miserable?
a: It leads to eternal death and damnation; the wages of sin is death.

q: Why are we free from death through Christ?
a: Because Christ redeemed us from sin, which leads to death

q: In Romans 7, Paul says a married woman is released from the law of marriage when what happens?
a: Her husband dies

q: According to Romans 7:4, through what did believers die to the law?
a: The body of Christ

q: In Romans 7:6, Paul says believers are released from the law so that they serve in what way?
a: The new way of the Spirit

q: What does every impure desire in our heart prove?
a: That we do not fear and love God as we should, and have broken His commandments.

q: What are the Commandments meant to do?
a: Show us our sin, lead us to repentance, and direct us to Christ

q: What does 'the old Adam in us' mean?
a: Our old sinful self—the sinful heart and inclination to evil with which we are born by nature

q: What benefits do they that are effectually called, partake of in this life?
a: They partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits which accompany or flow from them

q: What do you understand by the communion of saints?
a: Believers as Christ's members share in His treasures and gifts; everyone must use their gifts for others' benefit.

q: What is the communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ?
a: Partaking of the virtue of Christ's mediation in justification, adoption, sanctification, and whatever manifests union with him

q: What are the fruits or results of the Holy Spirit's work in us?
a: The forgiveness of sins and the resurrection of the body with life everlasting.

q: What is the indwelling of the Holy Spirit?
a: At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them

q: According to Romans 8:14, who are the sons of God?
a: All who are led by the Spirit of God

q: What is glorification?
a: God completing salvation: being made like Christ, receiving a glorified body, and sharing in Christ's glory as co-heirs

q: Which verse says, "And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him"?
a: Romans 8:28

q: Why does God sometimes permit suffering and trouble to come to His children?
a: To lead us to salvation and direct our whole life according to His gracious will

q: What did God the Father undertake in the covenant of grace?
a: To justify and sanctify those for whom Christ should die.

q: What does Romans 8:33 call the people God has chosen?
a: God's elect

q: In Romans 9:5, how does the Apostle Paul describe Jesus Christ?
a: As the one who is God over all, forever worthy of praise.

q: According to Romans 9:8, who are regarded as God's offspring, rather than the children of the flesh?
a: The children of the promise

q: Before Rebecca's twins were born or had done anything good or bad, what was she told about them?
a: “The older will serve the younger.”

q: Romans 9 says God's choice about the twins was not by works. What was it by?
a: By Him who calls

q: According to Romans 9:15-16, God's choosing does not depend on man's desire or effort, but on what?
a: God's mercy

q: How doth Christ make intercession?
a: By appearing in our nature before the Father, presenting his merit and sacrifice, and answering accusations against believers.

q: What way of salvation does the Law then point out to us?
a: It says, Keep the commandments and you shall be saved

q: What does the Bible contain?
a: Law telling us what we must do, and Gospel telling us how we are saved.

q: What does it mean to believe in Jesus Christ as our Lord?
a: To know by God's Word that Jesus Christ is our Lord and trust in Him with all our heart.

q: What is it to Believe on him?
a: To rest upon Him for Salvation

q: What is meant by "believing" the words "Given and shed for you for the forgiveness of sins"?
a: To heartily feel our sin and unworthiness, and confidently accept God's grace in Christ

q: What does faith include?
a: Knowledge of the Gospel facts, belief in the facts, and trust in Christ our Saviour.

q: Where is Christ offered?
a: In the Gospel

q: To which tribe did the apostle Paul belong?
a: Benjamin

q: In Romans 11, Paul says that at the present time there is a remnant chosen by what?
a: Grace

q: In Romans 11, Paul says that because of Israel's trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles. What is this meant to do to Israel?
a: Make Israel jealous

q: In Romans 11, why does Paul say the natural branches were broken off, while the Gentile believer stands?
a: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith

q: Is it possible to remain in the covenant of Baptism?
a: Yes; by the grace of God it is possible

q: In Romans 11, Paul says a hardening in part has come to Israel until what happens?
a: The full number of the Gentiles has come in

q: In Romans 11, Paul says that God's gifts and His call are what?
a: Irrevocable

q: What does 'communion' mean when we call the Church the communion of saints?
a: A congregation, a gathering of believers who form one body together.

q: In Romans 12:6-8, which gift is listed along with prophecy, serving, and teaching?
a: Encouraging

q: Why should we honor our rulers and government officials?
a: The State is God's servant to maintain law and order in the land.

q: Is the official who inflicts death penalty on criminals guilty of sin?
a: Not guilty; he does his duty as an officer of the State.

q: How should our behavior and manners be?
a: Modest and decent.

q: Did all mankind fall in Adam's first transgression?
a: All mankind, descending from Adam, sinned in him and fell with him

q: According to Romans 15:4, why was everything written in the past put in writing?
a: For our instruction, so that we might have hope

q: In Romans 15, Paul says he has fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ from Jerusalem all the way around to which region?
a: Illyricum

q: In Romans 15, to which country does Paul hope to travel by way of Rome?
a: Spain

q: In Romans 15, where is Paul going to serve the saints before he travels on to Rome and Spain?
a: Jerusalem

q: Which two regions were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem, according to Paul in Romans 15?
a: Macedonia and Achaia

q: Whom did Paul commend to the believers in Rome, asking them to welcome her in a manner worthy of the saints?
a: Phoebe

q: Which woman was a servant of the church in Cenchrea, commended by Paul in Romans 16?
a: Phoebe

q: In Romans 16, which two fellow workers in Christ Jesus does Paul say have risked their lives for him, so that all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them?
a: Prisca and Aquila

q: According to Romans 16:5, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia?
a: Epenetus

q: Whose mother does Paul greet in the letter to the Romans?
a: Rufus’

q: In Romans 16:18, what does Paul say people who cause divisions are serving instead of our Lord Christ?
a: Their own appetites

q: In Romans 16:20, what does Paul say the God of peace will soon do to Satan?
a: Crush him under your feet

q: In Romans 16, who identifies himself as the one who wrote down Paul's letter to the Romans?
a: Tertius

q: In Paul's closing greetings in Romans 16, what was Erastus's position in the city?
a: The city treasurer

q: In Romans 16:26, the mystery concealed for ages past has now been revealed in order to lead all nations to what?
a: The obedience that comes from faith

q: To which sinful, thriving Greek city did Paul write two well-known epistles?
a: Corinth

q: Can we ever be free from temptations in this world?
a: No; temptations must follow in this life, and we need them for our growth in God's kingdom

q: What do the names Holy, Christian, and Catholic express about the Church?
a: Holy—the Holy Spirit works in it; Christian—believers in Christ; Catholic—meant to include all men.

q: For how long has the Holy Spirit promised to keep believers in the faith?
a: Until the end of our lives, until the day of Jesus Christ.

q: Which epistle corrects disorder and division in a Greek church, including teaching on the Lord's Supper and spiritual gifts?
a: 1 Corinthians

q: In 1 Corinthians 1, who informed Paul that there were quarrels among the Corinthian believers?
a: Some from Chloe’s household

q: Do those believe in the only Saviour Jesus who seek their salvation and well-being from saints, in themselves, or anywhere else?
a: No, they deny that Jesus is the complete Saviour in whom all necessary salvation must be found

q: Paul thanks God that he did not baptize any of the Corinthians, except for which two men?
a: Crispus and Gaius

q: In 1 Corinthians 1, what does Paul say the message of the cross is to those who are being saved?
a: The power of God

q: In 1 Corinthians 1, what do Jews demand, according to Paul, while Greeks search for wisdom?
a: Signs

q: When Paul first came to the Corinthians, what did he resolve to know nothing except while he was with them?
a: Jesus Christ and Him crucified

q: Who is the Holy Spirit?
a: The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.

q: What is meant by the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit?
a: Our knowledge of Gospel truths becomes living and saving knowledge in our hearts

q: Why are believers in Christ called saints?
a: Because the Holy Spirit has sanctified them through faith in Christ.

q: How must God's Word be taught in the Church?
a: Without mixture of human thoughts and errors, just as God has given it.

q: Is baptism required to become a Christian?
a: Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family

q: In 1 Corinthians 3, what did Paul say the Corinthians' jealousy and dissension showed about them?
a: They were still worldly, walking in the way of man

q: What will happen to those who have received Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior at the end of the world?
a: The righteous will have glorified bodies, receive their reward, and dwell forever with the Lord

q: In 1 Corinthians 3, what does Paul say will reveal and prove the quality of each man's work on the foundation?
a: Fire, when the Day brings it to light

q: What did Paul say the fire will test on the Day of judgment?
a: The work each person has done

q: Why is the church called holy?
a: Because the Holy Spirit indwells it and sanctifies its members, despite their sins and shortcomings

q: How does 1 Corinthians 3:16 prove that the Holy Spirit is true God?
a: The Holy Spirit dwells in us; we are God's temple; therefore he must be true God

q: How will the bodies of believers rise at the Last Day?
a: Glorified, freed from sin, sickness, and infirmity, fashioned like Christ's glorious body.

q: What confession may every baptized person make about God and Christ?
a: God is my Father, Christ is my Redeemer, the Holy Spirit is my Sanctifier, and all benefits of Christ's redemption are mine

q: What is Christian stewardship?
a: Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants

q: In 1 Corinthians 4:2, what does Paul say is required of stewards?
a: That they be found faithful

q: When Paul told the Corinthians that he cared very little about being judged by them, who did he say is the one who judges him?
a: The Lord

q: In 1 Corinthians 4:7, Paul asks the Corinthians, "What do you have that you did not ..." what?
a: Receive

q: In 1 Corinthians 4, how does Paul say he became the father of the Corinthian believers?
a: Through the gospel

q: What common term describes believers being suddenly gathered to meet the Lord at His return?
a: The rapture

q: In 1 Corinthians 4, whom did Paul send to the Corinthians to remind them of his way of life in Christ Jesus?
a: Timothy, his beloved and faithful child in the Lord

q: In 1 Corinthians 4:20, what does Paul say the kingdom of God is not a matter of, but of power?
a: Talk

q: In 1 Corinthians 5:7, whom does Paul call "our Passover lamb" who has been sacrificed?
a: Christ

q: How do the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23) and the gifts of the Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:4-11) differ?
a: Fruit is Christlike character; gifts are abilities the Spirit gives for the common good

q: Why do you call Him our Lord?
a: Because He ransomed us, body and soul, from sin and the devil's power with His precious blood

q: Can those be saved who do not turn to God from their ungrateful and impenitent walk of life?
a: By no means. No unchaste person, idolater, adulterer, thief, greedy person, drunkard, slanderer, or robber shall inherit God's kingdom.

q: What does the Bible say about drunkards and the kingdom of God?
a: They will not inherit it

q: By what name do we call the Holy Spirit's work of making us holy?
a: Sanctification

q: According to 1 Corinthians 6:18, against what does the person who commits sexual immorality sin?
a: His own body

q: When do we defile God's temple?
a: When we use members of our body for filthy or immoral purposes.

q: What dreadful consequences often follow upon impurity of heart and life?
a: Ruined body, enfeebled mind, poisoned soul, tortured conscience, public shame, disease, and untimely death.

q: What does the Sixth Commandment command regarding purity in our deeds?
a: Flee sexual immorality, for our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit.

q: What does it mean that our body is a temple of the Holy Spirit?
a: Our bodies are God's temple and must not be given over to sin and impurity.

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, why does Paul say that a husband and wife may agree to a time of not coming together?
a: So they may devote themselves to prayer

q: In 1 Corinthians 7:9, whom does Paul tell to marry, since it is better to marry than to burn with passion?
a: Those who cannot control themselves should marry

q: What will be the state of the church in heaven?
a: It will be triumphant, because all its enemies are conquered

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, what command from the Lord does Paul give to a wife concerning her husband?
a: She must not separate from her husband

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, what should a believer do if an unbelieving spouse chooses to leave?
a: Let the unbeliever go

q: In 1 Corinthians 7:19, what does Paul say is what counts, since circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing?
a: Keeping God’s commandments

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, what does Paul tell a man who was a slave when he was called, if he can gain his freedom?
a: Take the opportunity

q: According to 1 Corinthians 7:22, what is a slave who was called by the Lord?
a: The Lord’s freedman

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, when Paul writes about virgins, what does he say he does not have from the Lord?
a: A command

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, if a person decides to marry despite Paul's advice to remain as he is, what does Paul say about that choice?
a: They have not sinned

q: In 1 Corinthians 7, what is the unmarried man concerned about?
a: The work of the Lord, and how to please the Lord

q: How long should husband and wife live together?
a: Until death parts them.

q: In 1 Corinthians 9, what does Paul call the Corinthians, saying they prove his apostleship in the Lord?
a: The seal of his apostleship

q: In 1 Corinthians 9, Paul asks whether he and which companion are the only apostles who must work for a living?
a: Barnabas

q: In 1 Corinthians 9, which three examples from everyday work does Paul give to show that workers deserve to benefit from their labor?
a: A soldier, a vineyard planter, and a shepherd

q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians 9, what has the Lord prescribed for those who preach the gospel?
a: That they should receive their living from the gospel

q: What does Paul say is his reward for preaching the gospel?
a: That he may offer the gospel free of charge

q: In 1 Corinthians 9, why does Paul say he makes himself a slave to everyone, though he is free of obligation to anyone?
a: To win as many as possible

q: In 1 Corinthians 9:25, Paul contrasts the crown that athletes in the games compete for with the crown believers seek. How does he describe the believers' crown?
a: It is imperishable

q: By what means can we put down evil lustful thoughts?
a: By God's Word and prayer.

q: What makes us certain that God will hear our prayer for help in temptation?
a: God is faithful and promised His help; He will not let us be tempted beyond what we can bear.

q: What does Paul call the cup that believers share at the Lord's Supper?
a: The cup of blessing

q: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
a: Examine themselves for knowledge to discern the Lord's body and faith.

q: Where has Christ promised that He will nourish and refresh believers with His body and blood as surely as they eat of this broken bread and drink of this cup?
a: At the institution of the Lord's Supper, and in Paul's words on sharing in Christ's body and blood.

q: Who does Paul say is head of the woman?
a: Man

q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians 11:3, who is the head of Christ?
a: God

q: What does Paul say about women’s long hair?
a: It is her glory; it is given to her as a covering

q: What do we receive in the Lord's Supper?
a: In and with the bread and the wine we receive the body and blood of Christ, which He gave up in death for us

q: How should we remember Christ's death?
a: We should fix our mind upon Christ's suffering and death to strengthen faith and love

q: Should the true doctrine of the Lord's Supper be rejected because it is mysterious and hard to understand?
a: No; it is a great comfort, and faith takes the Saviour at His word.

q: How often should we partake of the Lord's Supper?
a: Christ has not told us how often, but said, "do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."

q: Who are to come to the table of the Lord?
a: Those displeased with their sins who trust Christ's death covers them and want to strengthen faith and amend life.

q: What does Paul warn about eating the Lord's Supper in an unworthy way?
a: It brings judgment on that person

q: For whom is the Lord's Supper intended?
a: The Lord's Supper is intended for true Christians old enough and understanding enough to examine themselves

q: Is it of little importance how we receive the Lord's Supper?
a: By no means; we must be prepared to partake of these gifts worthily and not unworthily

q: Who partake of the Lord's Supper unworthily?
a: They who do not feel nor repent their sins, and who do not from their heart believe in Jesus

q: Do all communicants equally receive the benefits offered in the Lord's Supper?
a: The benefits are offered to all, but only believers receive them; the impenitent and unbelieving receive it to their condemnation.

q: According to 1 Corinthians 11, believers are told to examine themselves before doing what?
a: Partaking of the Lord's Supper (communion)

q: Who should partake of the Lord's Supper?
a: Only those who repent, believe in Christ for salvation, and love their fellow-men

q: What does the Third Article confess about our ability to believe in Christ?
a: We cannot by our own reason or strength believe in Christ or come to him

q: When the Holy Spirit calls us, what can we not do of ourselves?
a: We have neither the will nor the strength to come to Jesus

q: Why do we need the Holy Spirit for God's kingdom to come to us?
a: We cannot by our own strength believe in Christ; the Holy Spirit brings us to Him.

q: According to 1 Corinthians 12, are all believers expected to operate in every single gift of the Spirit?
a: No, the Spirit distributes different gifts to different members as one body

q: What term describes the belief that supernatural spiritual gifts, including healing and tongues, continue to operate in the church today?
a: Continuationism

q: How many gifts of the Spirit are listed in 1 Corinthians 12:8-10?
Which of these is one of the gifts of the Spirit listed in 1 Corinthians 12:8-10?
a: Message of wisdom

q: Which of these is NOT among the gifts of the Spirit listed in 1 Corinthians 12:8-10?
a: Showing mercy

q: Which chapter of 1 Corinthians lists nine gifts of the Spirit, including prophecy and healing?
a: 1 Corinthians 12

q: In 1 Corinthians 12:8, which gift is given to another by the same Spirit, alongside the message of wisdom?
a: The message of knowledge

q: Which spiritual gift involves an unusual measure of confident trust in God for the miraculous?
a: The gift of faith

q: Which spiritual gift involves speaking to others for their edification, encouragement, and comfort?
a: Prophecy

q: Which spiritual gift enables a believer to recognize whether a spirit at work is of God or not?
a: Distinguishing between spirits

q: Which spiritual gift is paired with tongues so that what is spoken in a tongue can be understood by the church?
a: Interpretation of tongues

q: Is the holy Christian church found in this place?
a: Yes; in the congregation, called in Scripture the body of Christ and the household of God

q: Who are the true members of the holy Christian Church?
a: Only true believers in Christ.

q: Which chapter of 1 Corinthians, right after the gifts are listed, is often called "the love chapter"?
a: 1 Corinthians 13

q: Where in the Bible is the well-known "love chapter" found, which says that love is patient and kind?
a: 1 Corinthians 13

q: What does it mean to put the best construction on everything?
a: To charitably explain his words and deeds in his favor, covering his faults.

q: Who said, “When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways”?
a: Paul

q: According to 1 Corinthians 14:2, the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to whom?
a: God

q: According to 1 Corinthians 14:4, whom does the one who speaks in a tongue edify?
a: Himself

q: According to 1 Corinthians 14, why should a tongue be interpreted in the church gathering?
a: To build up the church

q: In 1 Corinthians 14:19, Paul says that in the church he would rather speak how many coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue?
a: Five

q: In 1 Corinthians 14, what does Paul say will happen to an unbeliever who comes in while everyone is prophesying?
a: He will fall facedown and worship God

q: In 1 Corinthians 14, Paul teaches that tongues, when used publicly without interpretation, should be limited in the church for the sake of what?
a: Edification and order in the church

q: In 1 Corinthians 14, when a revelation comes to someone who is seated while a prophet is speaking in the church, what should the first speaker do?
a: He should stop speaking

q: According to 1 Corinthians 14:39, what does Paul say believers should not forbid?
a: Speaking in tongues

q: Why is it necessary to remain steadfast in God's Word?
a: To preserve our faith, do God's will, and endure unto our dying hour

q: According to 1 Corinthians 15:6, to how many brothers at once did the risen Jesus appear?
a: More than five hundred

q: In 1 Corinthians 15, Paul says that if Christ has not been raised, what is true of the apostles' preaching and the Corinthians' faith?
a: Both the preaching and the faith are worthless

q: In 1 Corinthians 15, Paul says that if the dead are not raised, what would he and the other preachers be exposed as?
a: False witnesses about God

q: What does it mean that Christ's body was glorified?
a: His glorified body was free from all human weakness, suffering, and death.

q: When shall we be completely victorious over temptation and evil?
a: At last, when our end approaches and the warfare is over, God gives victory.

q: Will the bodies of the dead be raised to life again?
a: Yes; 'the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable.'

q: In 1 Corinthians 16, to which city did Paul say the Corinthians' collection for the saints would be carried?
a: Jerusalem

q: In 1 Corinthians 16, in which city does Paul say he will stay until Pentecost?
a: Ephesus

q: Why does Paul say he will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost?
a: A great door for effective work has opened to him

q: According to Paul, who were the first converts in Achaia and devoted themselves to the service of the saints?
a: Stephanas and his household

q: In 1 Corinthians 16, how does Paul tell the Corinthians to greet one another?
a: With a holy kiss

q: Which book of the Bible comes immediately after 2 Corinthians?
a: Galatians

q: In 2 Corinthians 1:3, Paul calls God "the Father of compassion" and what else?
a: "the God of all comfort"

q: Why do you end your confession of faith with the word Amen?
a: Because I know that what I here confess is certainly true

q: In 2 Corinthians 2, what did Paul urge the Corinthians to do for the man who had been punished by the majority?
a: Forgive and comfort him, and reaffirm their love

q: What is the purpose of the devil, world, and flesh against us?
a: To hinder us from hallowing God's name and prevent His kingdom; to tempt us to oppose God's will.

q: When Paul went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ, why did he have no peace in his spirit?
a: He did not find his brother Titus there

q: In 2 Corinthians 2, what does Paul say the people who "peddle the word of God" are doing it for?
a: For profit

q: Was the covenant of grace always administered after one and the same manner?
a: The covenant of grace was not always administered the same way; Old Testament administrations differed from New Testament administrations.

q: The glory on Moses' face faded away. How does Paul say the glory of God's new way through the Spirit is different?
a: It is greater and lasts

q: What does it mean to put on Christ in Baptism?
a: We are clothed in the perfect righteousness Christ has merited for us.

q: In 2 Corinthians 4, Paul says he and his companions do not lose heart because of what God has given them?
a: This ministry, given in His mercy

q: In 2 Corinthians 4, whom does Paul say has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel?
a: The god of this age

q: In 2 Corinthians 4:7, what does Paul say we have "in jars of clay"?
a: This treasure

q: How do we serve our heavenly Father?
a: By using His gifts to help our neighbor, further His kingdom, and support His Church and Missions.

q: In 2 Corinthians 4:16, what is happening to our inner self day by day, even as the outer self wastes away?
a: It is being renewed

q: In 2 Corinthians 4:17-18, on what do Paul and his companions fix their eyes?
a: On what is unseen, which is eternal

q: What should we do with our old sinful nature?
a: It must be suppressed, subdued, and gradually destroyed through daily sorrow and repentance

q: What is regeneration?
a: New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction

q: In 2 Corinthians 6:2, Paul says that "now" is what, as he urges the Corinthians not to receive God's grace in vain?
a: The time of favor and the day of salvation

q: In 2 Corinthians 6, Paul describes his team as servants of God who live as "sorrowful, yet" what?
a: Always rejoicing

q: In 2 Corinthians 6:14, Paul says, "Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with ...?" Which word completes it?
a: Wickedness

q: Who was Paul writing to when he wrote, “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty”?
a: Corinthians

q: In 2 Corinthians 8, which churches did Paul say gave generously out of deep poverty and a terrible ordeal?
a: The churches of Macedonia

q: When the Macedonian churches gave to the saints, how much did Paul testify that they gave?
a: According to their ability and even beyond it

q: In 2 Corinthians 8, whom did Paul urge to help complete the Corinthians' act of grace, just as he had started it?
a: Titus

q: In Paul's appeal to the Corinthians, how did he say Jesus Christ made them rich?
a: Though He was rich, for their sakes He became poor

q: According to Paul, on what basis is a gift acceptable if the eagerness is there?
a: According to what one has, not what he does not have

q: In 2 Corinthians 8, whom does Paul thank God for putting the same devotion for the Corinthians into his heart?
a: Titus

q: In 2 Corinthians 8, who chose the brother praised for his work in the gospel to accompany Paul with the offering?
a: The churches

q: In 2 Corinthians 8, how does Paul describe Titus in relation to himself and the Corinthians?
a: His partner and fellow worker among them

q: In 2 Corinthians 9, Paul said he had been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year believers in which region were prepared to give?
a: Achaia

q: What benefits has Christ procured by His mediation?
a: Christ, by His mediation, has procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.

q: In 2 Corinthians 10, by whose mildness and gentleness does Paul appeal to the Corinthians?
a: Christ

q: In 2 Corinthians 10, Paul says that the weapons of his warfare have what power?
a: Divine power to demolish strongholds

q: According to Paul in 2 Corinthians 10, what do we do with every thought in spiritual warfare?
a: Take it captive to make it obedient to Christ

q: In 2 Corinthians 10, what did some in Corinth say about Paul's letters compared with his physical presence?
a: His letters are weighty and forceful, but his presence is unimpressive

q: In 2 Corinthians 10, what does Paul hope to do once the Corinthians' faith increases?
a: Preach the gospel in the regions beyond them

q: When Paul told the Corinthians he had promised them to one husband, to whom did he say he would present them as a pure virgin?
a: Christ

q: How does the devil tempt us?
a: The devil tempts us by putting evil thoughts into our minds

q: How does each of these enemies tempt us—the devil, the world, and our flesh?
a: Devil puts evil thoughts in our hearts; world tempts by example and threats; flesh urges sin.
